resources.name: Review before confirmation
resources.purpose: A clear review step before submitting important information.
resources.when: Adapt this public-service pattern to important actions: let users inspect and correct information before confirming.
resources.practice: Specify what can be reviewed, what can be changed and which action commits the request.

resources.name: Account connection & recovery
resources.purpose: Authentication interruptions, unavailable institutions and recovery.
resources.when: Useful for mapping account-linking exceptions with engineers. Plaid implementation and regional coverage are separate decisions.
resources.practice: Produce an exception matrix: trigger, user message, next action and owner.

resources.name: Arabic & bidirectional content
resources.purpose: Direction, mixed Arabic/Latin content and structural reading order.
resources.when: Use when specifying RTL behavior; pair the HTML guidance with platform-specific implementation checks.
resources.practice: Test amounts, dates, identifiers, wrapping and directional icons in one journey.

resources.name: Carbon design resources
resources.purpose: Component libraries and supporting design assets for complex products.
resources.when: Useful for enterprise patterns and library structure. Choose relevant public assets rather than importing everything.
resources.practice: Review a recurring pattern, then write usage guidance for your team.
resources.access: Public kits; Figma workspace plan applies

resources.name: Dense tables & batch actions
resources.purpose: Sorting, selection, expansion and actions over operational data.
resources.when: Use when a user needs to find, compare or act on many records.
resources.practice: Specify selection scope, permissions and the consequences of a batch action.

resources.name: Fluent 2 UI kits
resources.purpose: Code-aligned Figma libraries across web and native mobile.
resources.when: Useful for studying component structure, variable organization and platform differences.
resources.practice: Inspect one component's design properties alongside its implementation API.
resources.access: Public kit links; Figma workspace plan applies

resources.name: Checkout friction research
resources.purpose: Research on checkout steps, account selection and unnecessary effort.
resources.when: Use the public article to challenge checkout assumptions before adding more fields.
resources.practice: Map every required field to a real need; test guest and returning-user paths.
resources.access: Public article; wider research is paid

resources.name: Merchant admin patterns
resources.purpose: Shopify app layouts, resource indexes and task-oriented admin pages.
resources.when: Useful for merchant-facing products. These patterns target the Shopify ecosystem.
resources.practice: Compare an operational page against its resource-index and detail-page patterns.

resources.name: Microsoft HAX Toolkit
resources.purpose: Human-AI guidelines, examples, a workbook and failure-planning tools.
resources.when: Use before designing an AI feature to agree expectations, correction and recovery.
resources.practice: Run a focused team session and prioritize three interaction risks.

resources.name: People + AI Guidebook
resources.purpose: Mental models, explainability, feedback, control and graceful failure.
resources.when: Useful when users must understand or question uncertain AI output.
resources.practice: Define what the user sees, what they can correct and when human review is needed.

resources.name: Material 3 patterns
resources.purpose: A mobile-oriented reference for layouts, components and interaction.
resources.when: Use alongside the target platform's conventions and your team's brand system.
resources.practice: Compare a mobile flow at compact and expanded sizes before selecting a pattern.
resources.access: Public reference; linked kit access varies

resources.name: USWDS forms & design assets
resources.purpose: Accessible service patterns and official Figma/Sketch design assets.
resources.when: Useful for form-heavy, high-trust services; adapt to your product and jurisdiction.
resources.practice: Document one form's labels, validation, error summary and recovery.

resources.name: Tokens Studio for Figma
resources.purpose: Token organization, reusable values and optional external storage.
resources.when: Add when native variables no longer meet the agreed token workflow.
resources.practice: Pilot one token set with engineering and document its source of truth.
resources.access: Plugin available; some features require Pro

resources.name: Stark for Figma
resources.purpose: Accessibility inspection inside design files.
resources.when: Useful for contrast, focus-order and other design checks; verify the relevant plan and test the built product too.
resources.practice: Review one flow and attach findings to the design QA checklist.
resources.access: Free account entry; features vary by plan

resources.name: Iconify for Figma
resources.purpose: Search and import vector icons from multiple sets.
resources.when: Choose a consistent family and check the selected set's license.
resources.practice: Agree one family, size and direction rule instead of mixing styles.
resources.access: Public plugin; licenses vary by icon set

resources.name: WCAG 2.2 understanding
resources.purpose: Detailed accessibility explanations and associated techniques.
resources.when: Use to define acceptance criteria with engineering and accessibility specialists.
resources.practice: Translate relevant requirements into testable journey-level checks.

resources.name: WebAIM contrast checker
resources.purpose: Check foreground and background color pairs.
resources.when: Use for an immediate contrast check; a passing color pair is one part of accessibility.
resources.practice: Review actual token pairings, including error, disabled and muted content.

resources.name: Component contribution checklist
resources.purpose: An example of quality expectations across design, code, tests and documentation.
resources.when: Useful when proposing a component or defining what complete means.
resources.practice: Adapt the checklist to a component proposal with an owner and evidence.

resources.name: Storybook accessibility testing
resources.purpose: Accessibility checks within coded component stories.
resources.when: Partner with engineers when the team uses Storybook; combine automated checks with manual testing.
resources.practice: Ask for stories covering error and loading states, then review the results together.

resources.name: Design Tokens format
resources.purpose: A common exchange format from the Design Tokens Community Group.
resources.when: Useful when tokens need to move between tools. Confirm support in the chosen pipeline.
resources.practice: Agree names, aliases, owners and an export contract before automating.

resources.name: Figma Code Connect
resources.purpose: Connect design components to their real implementation.
resources.when: Useful when design and engineering maintain corresponding components; check plan access first.
resources.practice: Map one component, review its properties and document the mapping owner.
resources.access: Figma plan eligibility and engineering setup apply

resources.name: Figma MCP & agent workflows
resources.purpose: Supply design context to an AI agent and support structured Figma workflows.
resources.when: Use selected, well-structured frames and explicit rules; verify client access and permissions.
resources.practice: Pilot a bounded flow using existing components, then review layout, states and behavior.
resources.access: Supported client and Figma access limits apply

resources.name: Ten usability heuristics
resources.purpose: A shared vocabulary for finding interaction problems.
resources.when: Use to structure a critique, then validate important findings with user evidence.
resources.practice: Record an observable issue, its impact and a proposed check rather than a taste-based verdict.

resources.name: Research synthesis practice
resources.purpose: A practical approach to separating observations, findings and actions.
resources.when: Use after a research session to make evidence traceable and discuss it with the team.
resources.practice: Create an observation-to-finding-to-decision trail with evidence IDs.

resources.name: Consistent AI design with Design DNA
resources.purpose: Jack Roberts on the consistency problem: a design loop that critiques output against a reference, then codifies the winner into a reusable style.
resources.when: Use when AI-made designs look good once but drift or turn generic on the next run.
resources.practice: Pick one approved piece and list the ratios, colour coverage and refusals that make it work.

resources.name: Design DNA method
resources.purpose: A written method for turning one design into rules that can fail: relationships over values, one deliberate break, bans, tests and a rebuild from the spec.
resources.when: Use when writing a style specification an AI agent must reproduce across formats.
resources.practice: Rebuild a reference from your written rules alone, then list every difference as a missing rule.

resources.name: Scroll-driven website design with AI
resources.purpose: Nate Herk on a website skill that interviews for the visitor journey, builds scroll-led pages and screenshots its own work before review.
resources.when: Use when a marketing page needs a clear journey and a memorable moment rather than a template layout.
resources.practice: Write the journey section by section, mark where it should feel calm or intense, and name the one moment to remember.

resources.name: Design systems in the age of agents
resources.purpose: Cassie Groos (Hatch 2026) on agents as a third design-system consumer, context before components, and humans keeping judgment and accountability.
resources.when: Use when agents assemble UI from your system and the misses look polished but are not yours.
resources.practice: List the facts an agent had to guess in its last build, then decide where each should be written once.

resources.name: Component requirements document (CRD)
resources.purpose: One living, human-written and agent-readable document per component: testable requirement IDs, open markers, ruled-out options and dated decisions.
resources.when: Use when requirements, design notes and implementation decisions drift between documents.
resources.practice: Draft one CRD for an existing component and mark every unknown as open instead of guessing.

resources.name: Signs of AI writing
resources.purpose: A catalogue of patterns that make text read as machine-written: staged contrasts, reflex triads, inflated claims and filler.
resources.when: Use when reviewing interface copy, landing pages or emails drafted with AI.
resources.practice: Mark every pattern in one page of copy, then rewrite only those lines and compare.

resources.name: Savee
resources.purpose: A visual library for finding and saving design references across posters, layouts and brand work.
resources.when: Use to lock a visual reference before generating or designing, rather than starting from a written brief alone.
resources.practice: Collect three references for one brief and choose a single dominant direction.

resources.name: Refero
resources.purpose: Searchable styles, real product screens and user flows, with an MCP server for AI agents.
resources.when: Use for reference research on screens and flows before designing; connect the MCP when agents do the research.
resources.practice: Compare three shipped flows for one task and record what each does differently.
resources.access: Browsing available; MCP research needs a paid plan

resources.name: Higgsfield
resources.purpose: One account for many image and video generation models, available to agents through an MCP server and CLI.
resources.when: Use when a build needs custom imagery or motion that matches an agreed palette and style.
resources.practice: Generate one asset from a written style rule and check it against the reference.

resources.name: kie.ai
resources.purpose: A single API for many image and video models, used by the ScrollCraft skill for asset generation.
resources.when: Use when an agent workflow needs generated images or video through one key.
resources.practice: Budget one asset set, record the prompts used and review the output against the brand.

resources.name: Fish Audio
resources.purpose: Voice generation with a large voice library, emotion tags and an API for narration.
resources.when: Use for narrated motion graphics or product explainers.
resources.practice: Draft one 10-second narration, tag its emotional beats and review it with the visuals.
resources.access: Free tier; paid plans and API

resources.name: Claude workflow
resources.purpose: A practical operating workflow for Claude: task alignment, focused context, appropriate effort and observable verification.
resources.when: Use when briefing Claude or improving a team workflow across Claude Code, Cowork and chat. Commands depend on the client.
resources.practice: Take one recurring task, write its completion check and compare the result with the current approach.
resources.access: Free SKILL.md with supporting guides; no API key or plugin required

resources.name: Agent task brief
resources.purpose: Turn an unclear request into a useful brief with sources, constraints and acceptance checks.
resources.when: Use before substantial design, research or implementation work when the outcome or scope is unclear.
resources.practice: Brief one onboarding review using the existing component library and mark every material unknown.
resources.access: Free SKILL.md and editable Markdown template

resources.name: Agent context handoff
resources.purpose: Preserve decisions, evidence, file state and next actions across long sessions and handoffs.
resources.when: Use before compaction, a requested session transition or a change of approach after repeated failures.
resources.practice: Hand a bounded task to a teammate using the template, then check whether they can continue without repeating the audit.
resources.access: Free SKILL.md and editable Markdown template

resources.name: Agent extension review
resources.purpose: Assess an AI skill, plugin, mod or connector before adding it to a workflow.
resources.when: Use when an extension promises efficiency but its execution, access, context loading or maintenance cost is unclear.
resources.practice: Review one candidate at a named version and record what remains uninspected before recommending a pilot.
resources.access: Free SKILL.md and editable Markdown template; review does not install anything

resources.name: Website craft skill
resources.purpose: An agent workflow for websites: short interview, references, a design system page, anti-slop copy, build and screenshot verification.
resources.when: Use for any new or redesigned website or landing page built with an AI agent.
resources.practice: Run it on one page with real assets and review the screenshots section by section.
resources.access: Free SKILL.md for Claude Code, Codex and compatible agents

resources.name: Design loop skill
resources.purpose: Builds against a reference while separate critic passes check fidelity, brief, craft and AI tells until each passes.
resources.when: Use when a design must match a reference or keeps looking generic.
resources.practice: Run four rounds at most and keep the critic verdicts with the final screenshots.
resources.access: Free SKILL.md for Claude Code, Codex and compatible agents

resources.name: Design DNA skill
resources.purpose: Turns one approved design into a reusable style: dna.json, a short prompt, tests that can fail and a rebuild check.
resources.when: Use after a design is approved, or when a recurring format must stay consistent.
resources.practice: Codify one approved piece, then produce a second piece from the skill alone and compare.

resources.name: Agent-ready design system skill
resources.purpose: Sets up or audits a design system agents can build from: one origin per fact, tokens only, decision logs and drift reviews.
resources.when: Use when starting a growing product or when agents keep inventing components and values.
resources.practice: Audit one repository for raw values and undocumented variants, then rank fixes by guessing removed.

resources.name: Component CRD skill
resources.purpose: Writes and builds from a component requirements document, with testable IDs and open markers that stop a build.
resources.when: Use before designing or building a new component.
resources.practice: Write one CRD, generate tests from its IDs and record what design changed.

resources.name: ScrollCraft
resources.purpose: Nate Herk's skill for scroll-driven landing pages with layered heroes, a signature move and automated screenshot checks.
resources.when: Use when a page should feel like an experience: scrubbed video, pinned scenes or depth.
resources.practice: Build one section from your own photos first; add generated assets only if needed.
resources.access: MIT on GitHub; needs Node, ffmpeg and Playwright; generation uses a kie.ai key

resources.name: Humanizer
resources.purpose: A skill that rewrites AI-sounding text without changing what it says, based on Wikipedia's Signs of AI writing.
resources.when: Use as a final pass on any user-facing copy drafted with AI.
resources.practice: Run it on one page of copy and check that no facts changed.

resources.name: Refero design skill
resources.purpose: A research-first design workflow with bundled craft guides, using Refero's MCP for live references.
resources.when: Use for the reference and research step before designing.
resources.practice: Keep a client's own design system above the skill's defaults; record the references it chose.
resources.access: MIT on GitHub; live research needs Refero MCP

resources.name: Premium motion graphics with Claude
resources.purpose: Duncan Rogoff on five habits that lift AI-made promo videos: references, a written study, a motion design system, stills first and designer notes.
resources.when: Use when a promo or launch video made with an AI agent looks generic or off-brand.
resources.practice: Approve one still per scene type before rendering any video, and log every note as a rule.

resources.name: Prompt Motion
resources.purpose: A gallery of motion videos made with Claude, each posted with its full prompt, model and rendering stack.
resources.when: Use to find and compare motion references before writing a brief; take the feel, never the facts.
resources.practice: Study two detailed prompts and list the scenes, timing rules and bans each one specifies.

resources.name: AI film workflow with Claude skills
resources.purpose: Joey on building the world before the shots: story bible, locked characters, scene plates, then shot prompts, with a low-resolution draft pass.
resources.when: Use when AI-generated characters or scenes drift between generations, or credits run out on retries.
resources.practice: Draft one scene at 480p, review framing and dialogue, then render only the approved prompt at full resolution.
resources.access: Public video (22 min); sponsored by Higgsfield

resources.name: ElevenLabs
resources.purpose: Voice generation with multiple takes, word timings and an API for narration and captions.
resources.when: Use when a promo needs voiceover that captions and cuts can follow.
resources.practice: Generate four takes of one script and pick the best by listening, not by prompt.
resources.access: Free tier; paid plans and API

resources.name: Moises
resources.purpose: Audio separation that isolates or removes music, voice and instruments from a track.
resources.when: Use to remove unwanted background music from generated video audio before editing.
resources.practice: Separate one clip and check the dialogue stays clear after the music is removed.

resources.name: Motion graphics skill
resources.purpose: Coded motion promos: references, a motion design system, approved stills, then a frame-exact HTML build rendered with Playwright and ffmpeg.
resources.when: Use for product promos, launch films, UI motion and kinetic type built with an AI agent.
resources.practice: Render six stills, approve them, then the video, and keep a changelog of each review round.
resources.access: Free SKILL.md; needs Node, Playwright and ffmpeg

resources.name: AI film pipeline skill
resources.purpose: Runs an AI-generated film or ad in order: world bible, characters, scene plates, shot prompts, draft pass, final render and a credit log.
resources.when: Use for AI-generated ads, skits, music videos or character series.
resources.practice: Keep a production log of model, resolution and credits for every shot.
resources.access: Free SKILL.md; generation tools are paid

resources.name: AI film skills by Joey
resources.purpose: Five free skills: Story Bible Builder, Castkit characters, Scenecraft plates, Shotcaller for Seedance and Motiondojo for motion transfer.
resources.when: Use with the AI film pipeline when building characters, scenes and shot prompts for video models.
resources.practice: Lock one character face before building outfits or a character sheet.
resources.access: Free from the author on Higgsfield

resources.name: 23 Claude workflow mistakes
resources.purpose: Jay E / RoboNuggets discusses habits that affect context, output quality and usage.
resources.when: Use as a discussion starter; check changing product details against current documentation. The companion PDF requires community access.
resources.practice: Pick one relevant habit, propose a bounded workflow change and verify it on your own task.
resources.access: Public video and transcript; linked community guide has separate access

resources.name: Claude Code working practices
resources.purpose: Official guidance on task context, verification, session management and reusable workflows.
resources.when: Use when defining how a team briefs and checks agent-assisted implementation work.
resources.practice: Choose one real task and define a completion check that the agent can actually run.
resources.access: Public Anthropic documentation; commands require a compatible Claude Code version

resources.name: Claude usage and context costs
resources.purpose: Official guidance for interpreting usage, cache statistics and context costs.
resources.when: Use when a workflow consumes unexpected usage or a proposed optimization needs evidence.
resources.practice: Record the client, model, available usage data and output quality before changing one workflow variable.
resources.access: Public Anthropic documentation; subscription usage and API estimates differ

resources.name: MCP connector setup and trust
resources.purpose: Official reference for connecting tools, inspecting access and understanding tool discovery.
resources.when: Use before proposing a new connector or changing a team integration.
resources.practice: Compare one bounded connector use case with the existing workflow and document permissions and a rollback path.
resources.access: Public Anthropic documentation; workspace and provider permissions apply
